analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the speaker, לְנֹחַ identifies Noah as the addressee, and the imperative בֹּא (“enter”) begins the direct speech. The later verb רָאִיתִי means “I have seen.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה לְנֹחַ, “Yahweh said to Noah,” יַהְוֶה names the speaker who commands Noah to enter the ark.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה לְנֹחַ, לְ marks Noah as the person Yahweh addresses. The command בֹּא אַתָּה וְכָל־בֵּיתְךָ tells him to enter the ark with his household.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine singular personal name.

analysis.evidence: YHWH addresses Noah directly. The singular imperative בֹּא addresses אַתָּה (“you”), וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ includes his whole household in the command, and אֶל הַתֵּבָה identifies the ark as the place they are to enter.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: The singular imperative בֹּא addresses Noah. The explicit אַתָּה singles him out, and וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ adds his whole household to the command to enter the ark.
analysis.morphology: Independent second-person masculine singular pronoun, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: you, as for you (the one addressed set apart)

analysis.evidence: In אַתָּה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ, “you and your whole household,” כָל stands in construct with בֵּיתְךָ and includes the entire household in the command to enter the ark.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus masculine singular construct noun כָל.

analysis.evidence: In בֹּא אַתָּה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ אֶל הַתֵּבָה, אֶל introduces הַתֵּבָה as the place Noah and his household are commanded to enter.

draft.change: Add the feminine noun תֵּבָה under its own consonants, תבה. The supplied gentilic gloss and root תאר do not account for the vessel in this passage.
draft.definition: A container that carries its occupants on water, here the ark that Noah and his household enter.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:1 identifies the ark by who must enter it. Genesis 7:17–18 shows the rising water lifting it until it floats.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 7:1, בֹּא commands Noah to enter, and אֶל הַתֵּבָה names his destination. The definite article points back to the vessel Noah was told to build in Genesis 6:14 and enter with his family in Genesis 6:18.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed definite article הַ־ with doubling of the following ת, on a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: The vessel that carries Noah and his household on the floodwaters.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the command to enter the ark. In אֹתְךָ רָאִיתִי צַדִּיק, the speaker tells Noah, “I have seen that you are righteous.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Gen.7.1 to the existing object-pronoun sense as an example of a second-person singular object placed before its verb.
draft.definition: With a pronominal suffix, אֵת expresses the direct object separately from the verb.
draft.evidence: In Gen.7.1, אֹתְךָ precedes רָאִיתִי, “I have seen.” Its masculine singular suffix identifies Noah, the addressee, as the object.

analysis.evidence: Yahweh addresses Noah. In אֹתְךָ רָאִיתִי צַדִּיק, “I have seen you to be righteous,” אֹתְךָ places Noah before the verb as the person Yahweh has seen, and צַדִּיק describes him.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the suffixed form אֹת־ with the second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ־ךָ.

analysis.evidence: אֹתְךָ (“you”) is the direct object of רָאִיתִי, and צַדִּיק (“righteous”) describes what YHWH has perceived about Noah. YHWH gives this assessment as the reason for telling Noah to enter the ark with his household.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: In אֹתְךָ רָאִיתִי צַדִּיק לְפָנַי, Yahweh tells Noah, “I have seen that you are righteous before me.” צַדִּיק describes Noah, and לְפָנַי identifies Yahweh as the one who judges his conduct.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective, used predicatively of Noah.
analysis.sense: righteous (of a man): doing right before God

analysis.evidence: Yahweh is speaking. In אֹתְךָ רָאִיתִי צַדִּיק לְפָנַי, he says that he has found Noah righteous in his sight. The suffix refers to Yahweh as the one judging Noah.
analysis.morphology: Compound preposition formed from לְ and the plural construct of פָּנִים, with a first-person singular suffix.
analysis.sense: before, in the presence of (a person, Yahweh)

analysis.evidence: In בַּדּוֹר הַזֶּה, “in this generation,” הַזֶּה points to Noah’s own generation. YHWH describes Noah as righteous among his contemporaries.
analysis.gloss: among the people of the generation
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ, followed by a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: generation, the people alive at one time

draft.change: Add Genesis 7:1 as an example of the existing this-with-noun sense in zeh.
draft.definition: After a definite noun, זֶה points out the particular person or thing in view.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:1 uses בַּדּוֹר הַזֶּה for the generation to which Noah belongs.

patch.value: "Like the Arabic cognate, the older Ugaritic form is ḏ (1.24:45), but Standard Ugaritic uses forms in d"; § 57.3: "can also be used as a conjunction".
"the relative pronoun". "From דִּי, ultimately from Proto-Semitic *ḏV- ('this')".
"this, that"; הָדֵן "= הָא ד׳"; מן קדמת דנא "ere this, formerly".
"(cmp. דָּא with formative ך) this, that. Ezra V, 16".

Root question: no verbal or nominal root was found. The word is the Semitic pointing (deictic) element *ḏ-, with vowel endings for gender and case (Arabic ḏā, ḏī, ḏū; Ugaritic d/ḏ, f. dt; Sabaic ḏ-, ḏn; Ge'ez zə, za, Aramaic dā, dī, dənā; Phoenician z, zn), found in every branch; scripture has no noun or verb זהה/זוה/זיה from which it could have grown, and Arabic grammarians' reconstructions of ذَا as ذَوَى or ذَيَى (Lane p. 947) only fit it to the root pattern. The later Hebrew verb זִהָה "identify" is formed from זֶה, not the reverse. So the entry is keyed by its own consonants, זה, and the evidence for the pointing word itself is as strong as for any Semitic word. One pointer serves as demonstrative and relative across the languages (Hebrew זוּ and poetic זֶה, Aramaic דִּי, Ugaritic d, Sabaic ḏ-, Ge'ez za, Old Byblian z, Arabic ḏū in Ṭayyiʾ), which is why the relative words are kept here. Not this element: Hebrew שֶׁ־ and Akkadian ša (Akkadian keeps ḏ as z, so ša does not answer to ḏ; Wiktionary's comparison of ša with ذَا is not followed); אֵלֶּה "these" and Aramaic אִלֵּין (another pointing word, ʾl); Syriac ܗܳܢܳܐ "this" (hn); the month name זִו (זיו "brightness"). BDB files זֹאת under זֶה (g.ah.aa); its cross-reference key g.ab.ad has no tokens and is claimed here. g.ai.aa and g.aj.aa list the same two tokens of זוֹ (Hos 7:16, Psa 132:12); both keys are on זֹה, so they are counted twice there. Zec 2:8 and Psa 68:9 are cited by the Hebrew numbering (English 2:4, 68:8); Dan 4:14, 4:22, 4:27, 4:29 and 6:11 likewise (English 4:17, 4:25, 4:30, 4:32, 6:10). Not consulted: CAL (refuses automated access), DULAT, Leslau, Old Aramaic inscriptions (znh, zy). Dillmann's column numbers were read from the Internet Archive OCR and should be checked on the page image. זֶה סִינַי is left open between a title ("the One of Sinai") and "this Sinai". The particle's senses are illustrative, not exhaustive: about 1,800 tokens.

value.note: In בַּדּוֹר הַזֶּה, “in this generation,” the demonstrative follows דּוֹר and points to Noah's own generation.

patch.value: מִזֶּה אֶחָד וּמִזֶּה אֶחָד: "from this side and from that", holding up Moses' hands.
וְקַרְנָא דִכֵּן וְעַיְנִין לַהּ: "that horn which had eyes".
הָדֵא דִּיַתִקִא: "this is the covenant", Jer 31:33's זֹאת הַבְּרִית.

analysis.evidence: In בַּדּוֹר הַזֶּה, “in this generation,” הַזֶּה follows דּוֹר and agrees with it in gender, number and definiteness. It points to the generation in which Yahweh has seen Noah to be righteous.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular demonstrative pronoun with the prefixed definite article הַ־, used attributively after its noun.
